about: Test window, the test split only: test-break session B's B2, recorded after the freeze (8c7b2f6); no replay, sweep, or tuning on it except the test sweep. A downstream_timeout break at 04:11:07 (payments-api degraded), left to end with the fault's 390 s lifetime, never cleared by hand, with the alarm rule off: no agent run. The latency alarm alone went into ALARM, at 04:11:48, and was OK at 04:18:08; the pool-wait and errors alarms never fired. payments-api records no change, so the deploy history holds no culprit; nothing changed in the 10 minutes before the onset. A distractor in the 180-minute log reach: B1, the db_pool_exhaustion break of 02:30:52 (POOL_MAX_SIZE 20 to 2, reverted at 02:37:23; pool wait into ALARM 02:31:21, latency 02:34:48, errors 02:35:26, OK 02:35:36, ALARM again 02:35:46, all OK by 02:37:38), 100 minutes before the onset. The deploy history shows B1's revert and pool change, decoys LOG_SAMPLE_RATE 0.1 to 0.25 at 00:31:06 and RECOMMENDATIONS_ENABLED false to true at 00:07:15, then session A's records. Every deploy record dated before the alarm had been written by then.
account: 123456789012 stands in for the account ID wherever AWS wrote it.
